Treat yourself to a spine-haunting good time of frights into the night!

Fright by Night Operating Hours:

October 2 – November 1

Fridays: 6pm – 10pm

Saturdays: 2pm – 10pm

Sundays: 2pm – 10pm

BOOVILLE

Extra Weekend – Booville Opens One Week Early!

Fun for the whole family!

Festive fall fun activities, trick-or-treating, face-painting and entertainment await the little ghouls and goblins. events.summary: Picha Farms is ready for you to come and enjoy some fall family fun on the farm.
events.description:
Picha Farms is ready for you to come and enjoy some fall family fun on the farm.
Here are the fun fall activities you get to experience:

• Corn Maze — Picha Farms is celebrating our spider friends in our corn maze! You’ll stroll through the web, in search of answers to eight trivia questions. A free mini pumpkin awaits you at the exit as a reward for all your hard work.
• Hayride — Relax and enjoy the fresh air as you meander through wide-open fields of pumpkins.
• Slingshot — Hit your target and win $5 off your pumpkin purchase.
• Food — Sip on a latte or hot apple cider; munch on kettle corn, enjoy gourmet hot dogs, hamburgers, tacos, potatoes and much more from our awesome vendors.
• Fall Décor — With over 25 varieties of pumpkins to choose from, grab a wheelbarrow and stroll through the wide-open spaces. You have over 9-acres to search and find your perfect pumpkin. And don’t forget to stalk up on gourds and cornstalks.
• If you’d like to celebrate a birthday in our birthday tent, the rental is $60 for 2 hours, including set up and clean up time. Pumpkin coupons and tickets to the maze, hayride, slingshot and kiddie train are available for purchase in our stand. (Groups wishing to gather in our party tent are also welcome to reserve a time.)

Check the Facebook page for updates.

6140 Guide Meridian Rd, Lynden, WA, 98264
events.summary: If you love the Fall, and you love apples, you’ll want to visit Bellewood Farms this harvest season.
events.description:
If you love the Fall, and you love apples, you’ll want to visit Bellewood Farms this harvest season. You’re invited to join in the fall festivities beginning Saturday, Sep 5th, running through the Fall. Beat the weekend crowds and come on a weekday.

Bellewood Farms is the largest apple orchard in western Washington, with over 24 varieties and specializing in the best Honeycrisp apples on the planet. Come pick your own apples for a fun farm experience. Our pumpkin patch opens Sep 26th and is the largest in Whatcom County.

U-pick Apples: Experience picking your own fresh fruit when the orchard opens on 9/5, starting off with Tsugaru apples, a farm favorite. Other varieties will follow each week. Our Farmstore also has the best of the crop apples, clean and ready to take home. Check back here for info on u-pick varieties:

9/5-13 Tsugaru Apples

Tasty Food: Enjoy a special harvest breakfast and lunch menu in our Ten Mile Cafe and Bakery. Featuring apple cider slushies, local beers and hard cider, and Lynden’s best cinnamon rolls.

Fun Gifts: Grab some fun gifts in our Farmstore where we carry wide varieties of apples and cider and Caramel apples, and our famous Honey Roasted Peanut Butter

Bin Rides: Travel out to the orchard on a tractor pulled bin train (nominal charge). Or get some fresh air and walk out to the orchard for a healthy family experience.

School Tours (weekdays only): Reserve a spot for your Whatcom County school. We love sharing with kids and the community…

events.summary: Every year at our annual convention, GeekGirlCon sets up an inclusive environment at the heart of downtown Seattle.
events.description:
Every year at our annual convention, GeekGirlCon sets up an inclusive environment at the heart of downtown Seattle. Together, we celebrate and honor the legacies of under-represented groups in science, technology, comics, arts, literature, game play, and game design.

events.description:
(All Ages) Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos) is a vibrant Mexican tradition that honors and celebrates the lives of loved ones who have passed away, and October 27 – November 2 are special days dedicated to remember the spirits of our animal companions. While our pets and animal friends may no longer walk beside us, their presence remains deeply felt, and this is a day to honor that connection. The tradition is rooted in pre-Hispanic Indigenous rituals and has evolved through the years.

An ofrenda, or “offering” is a beautifully decorated altar meant to welcome spirits home. We will be celebrating the lives of past farm animals, and if you would like to participate bring a picture of one of your favorite animals from the farm, draw a photo of them, or write a letter to them. You may also bring a photo of your deceased pet or animal to add to the altar. We will keep the ofrenda up overnight, and photos maybe be picked up by November 2.

If you would like to create an ofrenda at home here’s how:

Select a place for your alter that was meaningful to your pet, and where you can safely place items
Place a photo of your pet at the center of the alter, or draw a picture of their likeness, or write their name on a piece of paper surrounded by hearts
Include their favorite things, like a collar, a favorite toy, or a small treat
Candles help light their way home
Marigolds bright colour and scent are said to guide the spirits back
Water will refresh them after their long jouney…

If you love the Fall, and you love apples, you’ll want to visit Bellewood Farms this harvest season. You’re invited to join in the fall festivities beginning Saturday, Sep 5th, running through the Fall. Beat the weekend crowds and come on a weekday.

Bellewood Farms is the largest apple orchard in western Washington, with over 24 varieties and specializing in the best Honeycrisp apples on the planet. Come pick your own apples for a fun farm experience. Our pumpkin patch opens Sep 26th and is the largest in Whatcom County.

U-pick Apples: Experience picking your own fresh fruit when the orchard opens on 9/5, starting off with Tsugaru apples, a farm favorite. Other varieties will follow each week. Our Farmstore also has the best of the crop apples, clean and ready to take home. Check back here for info on u-pick varieties:

9/5-13 Tsugaru Apples

Tasty Food: Enjoy a special harvest breakfast and lunch menu in our Ten Mile Cafe and Bakery. Featuring apple cider slushies, local beers and hard cider, and Lynden’s best cinnamon rolls.

Fun Gifts: Grab some fun gifts in our Farmstore where we carry wide varieties of apples and cider and Caramel apples, and our famous Honey Roasted Peanut Butter

Bin Rides: Travel out to the orchard on a tractor pulled bin train (nominal charge). Or get some fresh air and walk out to the orchard for a healthy family experience.

School Tours (weekdays only): Reserve a spot for your Whatcom County school. We love sharing with kids and the community…

Farmers markets are an essential part of our economy and community. Shopping at farmers markets helps to support agricultural producers, ensured food access for all and builds connections between producers and consumers.

DETAILS:

• The market is open every Thursday.

• Winter Market is open 10am - 4pm (Nov-Apr)

• Summer Market is open 10am - 6pm (May-Oct)

• Most vendors accept and prefer cash but can also process credit and debit cards. You can purchase market tokens with your card at the information booth to use for purchase at all booths. We can also process your Community Gift e-Card - Buy Here

• EBT is accepted! Inquire at the main tent to see how you can receive up to $10 with the SNAP Market Match program

• Enjoy Live Music and Food Tents during the Summer (May to October)

• Vendors rotate often and seasonally, no week is every the same as that last: fruits, vegetables and seasonal produce, jams, honey, preserves, kombucha, baked goods, fresh flowers, cheese, bath and body products, house plants and potted plants, gems & stones, gifts, wine, meat, snacks and art (jewelry, glass works, yard art, cloth and textile crafts, face)

• Pets are allowed on leash

events.title: Dia de los Muertos in Seabrook
events.placeLines:
Seabrook, Washington
4275 SR 109, Seabrook, WA, 98571
events.summary: Celebrate Día de los Muertos in Seabrook on Friday, October 30 and Saturday, October 31 with a weekend of creativity, remembrance, and community.
events.description:
Celebrate Día de los Muertos in Seabrook on Friday, October 30 and Saturday, October 31 with a weekend of creativity, remembrance, and community. Rooted in Mexican traditions honoring loved ones who have passed, the celebration brings families together through a community ofrenda, hands-on workshops, music, dance, and a Marigold Candlelight Procession through town.

Special thanks to event sponsor Our Secret Garden for generously sharing their time, talents, and cultural knowledge to help bring the traditions of Día de los Muertos to life in Seabrook.

Friday: Community Creation Day

1:00–6:00 PM at Town Hall

Preparing for Día de los Muertos is part of the celebration itself. In many Mexican communities, families and neighbors gather to create decorations, prepare offerings, and share stories of loved ones.

Join us at Town Hall to take part in that spirit of togetherness. Make paper marigolds, craft papel picado, decorate memory butterflies, and help build Seabrook’s community ofrenda, a shared altar of remembrance.

Guests are invited to bring a photo or memory of someone they love to contribute to the ofrenda while helping create the colorful pieces that will become part of Saturday’s celebration. All ages are welcome, and no crafting experience is needed.

Saturday: Día de los Muertos Celebration

Saturday’s celebration brings the community together at Town Hall and along Market Street for an afternoon and evening of remembrance, art, music, and dance.

Trick or treat around our habitats to snatch some candy or a non-snack prize while learning about the mesmerizing (and sometimes mysterious) marine world. Costumes are welcome!

38625 SE King St, Snoqualmie, WA, 98065
events.summary: Every October, the Northwest Railway Museum invites families to ride the train or drive up to the Train Shed Exhibit Hall for some extra-special,…
events.description:
Every October, the Northwest Railway Museum invites families to ride the train or drive up to the Train Shed Exhibit Hall for some extra-special, family-friendly, harvest time fun. The passenger coaches are adorned with autumn foliage, slightly spooky decor can be found all around the Train Shed Exhibit Hall and the Snoqualmie Depot, and on the weekends families can enjoy hot cider and live cider pressing demonstrations. Costumes encouraged for visitors of all ages!

Learn how the railway changed everything – including agriculture!

Halloween Train is just shy of 2-hours round-trip and departs from Snoqualmie Depot and North Bend Depot.

You will first ride up to Snoqualmie Falls to see the scenic view of the Snoqualmie River Valley from the train, next you will ride to the Railway History Campus (RHC) for a half-hour visit.

In and around the Train Shed Exhibit Hall will be a bunch of activities! A volunteer will do cider press demonstrations, and may ask for a hand from one of the visitors. Nearby, Museum staff will have apple peeling and coring tools to try out. Inside the Train Shed, you will find crafts, plenty of photo opportunities, and live music performed by Eric Ode!

Thirsty? You can find hot cider available inside the Railway Education Center classroom just across the courtyard. There will also be historic toys and games available to play!

The train horn will sound four times to let you know when it is time to board the train for your return ride. If you want…

events.place: El Centro de la Raza, Seattle
events.placeLines:
El Centro de la Raza, Seattle
2524 16th Ave S, Seattle, WA, 98144
events.summary: @ El Día de los Muertos (The Day of the Dead) is a time to remember and honor those who have passed.
events.description:
@

El Día de los Muertos (The Day of the Dead) is a time to remember and honor those who have passed. At El Centro de la Raza, we honor social justice heroes, victims of racially motivated violence, those whose lives were lost too soon, and community members whose lives made a lasting impact. As El Centro de la Raza celebrates 54 years of building the Beloved Community, our exhibit honors more than five decades of work for human rights, social services, and political and environmental justice. Our unique Día de los Muertos exhibit connects remembrance with current and historic social justice issues in our community, nation, and world, honoring those who came before us while inspiring the work still ahead.

Día de los Muertos Opening Celebration
Sunday, November 1, 2026 | 12:00–5:30 P.M.

Join El Centro de la Raza as we celebrate the 21st Annual Día de los Muertos. This year’s theme, Raíces que Nos Unen (Roots That Unite Us), honors those who came before us and celebrates the invisible roots that connect us through memory, culture, family, and community.

Experience beautiful, community-created ofrendas, art, music, and traditions as we remember our loved ones and honor those whose lives continue to inspire us to build a more just, compassionate, and connected community.

Together, we honor the past, celebrate the present, and strengthen the future.

events.summary: Auburn, Washington has been designated by the Veterans Day National Committee and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as a Regional Site for the 2026…
events.description:
Auburn, Washington has been designated by the Veterans Day National Committee and the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as a Regional Site for the 2026 celebration of Veterans Day.

The City of Auburn is proud to be a Vietnam War Commemorative Partner and considers it an honor and privilege to host this annual event. Auburn has hosted the Veterans Parade since 1965. The 2026 parade marks our 61st year! Over time, the parade has grown into one of the largest parades of its kind in the United States of America.

The purpose of Auburn’s Veterans Parade & Observance is to positively focus on honoring our country’s veterans and active military personnel. Recognition is focused on congressionally recognized Veteran Service Organizations and their auxiliaries, the military and military reserve, National Guard, and ROTC. The goal of Auburn’s Veterans Parade & Observance is to honor to our country’s veterans and to their military missions of defending freedom around the world.

The 61st annual Veterans Parade will be held in Auburn on Saturday, November 7, 2026 starting at 11:00 AM. The parade typically boasts over 120 units and nearly 4,000 parade participants, including more than 10 marching bands, numerous military vehicles, veterans’ units, honor guards and more.

The parade route travels west along Main Street from E Street to A Street NW/SW. The day-long activities run from 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM.

305 Harrison St, Seattle, WA, 98109
events.summary: Diwali: Lights of India will take place November 7, 2026 in the Armory Food & Event Hall.
events.description:
Diwali: Lights of India will take place November 7, 2026 in the Armory Food & Event Hall. The festival is part of the Seattle Center Festál series. It is free and open to the public.

Seattle Center Festál presents Diwali: Lights of India in partnership with Northwest Share. This year’s festival features music, dance, visual art, martial arts, a cooking demonstration and more.

HISTORY

Diwali (Festival of Lights) is a major cultural celebration observed throughout India every fall. It symbolizes the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance. Light is a metaphor for knowledge and consciousness. During Diwali in India, houses and business locations are brightly illuminated with lamps, diyas (oil lamps), and candles. Lakshmi, the Goddess of Wealth, is worshiped for prosperity. Diwali is celebrated with families and friends, wearing new clothes, partaking in family feasts, enjoying delicious sweets, sharing gifts and most importantly, setting off firecrackers!

Farmers markets are an essential part of our economy and community. Shopping at farmers markets helps to support agricultural producers, ensured food access for all and builds connections between producers and consumers.

• Summer Market is open 10am - 6pm (May-Oct)

• EBT is accepted! Inquire at the main tent to see how you can receive up to $10 with the SNAP Market Match program

• Pets are allowed on leash

With European and local vendors, holiday karaoke, Santa meetings, festive drinks and more, there’s a little something for everyone.

According to centuries-old tradition, many German towns host Christmas Markets in December; each one is unique, featuring local artisans and festive regional refreshments. events.title: Donkey Creek Chum Fest
events.placeLines:
Donkey Creek Park, Gig Harbor
8714 Harborview Dr, Gig Harbor, WA, 98332
events.summary: Every year, the greater Gig Harbor community celebrates the return of salmon to our local waters.
events.description:
Every year, the greater Gig Harbor community celebrates the return of salmon to our local waters. The Donkey Creek Chum Festival serves to remind us that the quality of our water, and the habitat it supports, connects us all.

Participants will start their walk at Austin Park along Harborview Drive where they will receive a Salmon Passport. They will visit booths with activities and information for kids and adults along the trail through txʷaalqəł Estuary, behind the Harbor History Museum, and ending in Donkey Creek Park. Completed passports should be turned in to the front desk at the Harbor History Museum by 2pm on the day of the event to be entered into a drawing for a salmon-themed prize.

The goal of our salmon festival is to bring people together to promote sustainability, sound environmental stewardship, preservation of our maritime history and culture, responsible recreation, habitat preservation, and shoreline restoration — one salmon at a time. Join us on November 15th as we recognize new ways to improve and protect our waterways!

This event is free and open to people of all ages and abilities. The trail is less than 0.25 in length on a gravel packed pathway. Free public parking is available at the Museum, along Harborview Drive and Austin Street.

events.placeLines:
Quest Church, Seattle
1401 NW Leary Way, Seattle, 98107
events.summary: Step right up, Seattle!
events.description:
Step right up, Seattle!

Kinship Collaborative invites you to HULLABALOO!, a joyful celebration of queer art and belonging. This spectacular afternoon, we’re bringing together an eclectic lineup of drag, circus arts, comedy, ventriloquism, and plenty of unexpected delights to create a world where being different is something to put in the spotlight.

HULLABALOO! is a celebration of what can happen when we make room for one another to show up fully and share the wonderfully weird things that make us who we are.

Because under this big top, you don’t have to be like everyone else to belong.

Join us at HULLABALOO!
Saturday, November 21, 2026
Doors at 1 PM | Show at 2 PM
Quest Church | Seattle, WA

Benefiting the Queer Seattle Prosperity Fund

The fun starts before the show!

Come early and join HULLABALOO! before the curtain goes up! Doors open at 1 PM with pre-show interactive experiences.

Featuring Zack Binder & Ticklemuff!

Zack Binder (he/him) is a trans masculine ventriloquist comedian and actor. Originally from Toronto, Zack began his performance career in Canada as Drag King ZacKey Lime. Zack retired from drag during the pandemic and began pursuing his other love, acting. In 2021, he worked as Elliot Page’s stand in on Season 3 of The Umbrella Academy. When the season wrapped, Zack packed his bags and drove to LA. Little did he know that two years later, he would find himself playing the recurring role of Derek for three episodes in Season 4 of the popular Netflix show.…

events.description:
Burien Farmer’s Market

Farmers markets are an essential part of our economy and community. Shopping at farmers markets helps to support agricultural producers, ensured food access for all and builds connections between producers and consumers.

(Inclement weather rule in-effect: if there is snow present and/or temperature is below 20 degrees, the farmer’s market will be closed. We will post signs at Town Square and on Social Media)

DETAILS:

• The market is open every Thursday.

• Winter Market is open 10am - 4pm (Nov-Apr)

• Summer Market is open 10am - 6pm (May-Oct)

• Most vendors accept and prefer cash but can also process credit and debit cards. You can purchase market tokens with your card at the information booth to use for purchase at all booths. We can also process your Community Gift e-Card - Buy Here

• EBT is accepted! Inquire at the main tent to see how you can receive up to $10 with the SNAP Market Match program

• Enjoy Live Music and Food Tents during the Summer (May to October)

• Vendors rotate often and seasonally, no week is every the same as that last: fruits, vegetables and seasonal produce, jams, honey, preserves, kombucha, baked goods, fresh flowers, cheese, bath and body products, house plants and potted plants, gems & stones, gifts, wine, meat, snacks and art (jewelry, glass works, yard art, cloth and textile crafts, face)

• Pets are allowed on leash

events.title: Garden d’Lights $5 Night & Sensory Friendly Night
events.placeLines:
Garden Grounds, Bellevue
12001 Main Street, Bellevue, 98005
events.summary: Sensory Friendly Night Enjoy Garden d’Lights in a quieter setting.
events.description:
Sensory Friendly Night

Enjoy Garden d’Lights in a quieter setting. All lights will be on as usual, but there will be no live music, and attendance is limited to half capacity (200 guests per half-hour) to create a calmer experience. Tickets are required.

Garden d’Lights is a dazzling holiday tradition that transforms the Bellevue Botanical Garden into a magical wonderland, featuring over half a million sparkling lights in whimsical shapes of plants, flowers, birds, animals, and cascading waterfalls.

Set amid the Garden’s natural beauty, this beloved, family-friendly event has enchanted visitors for decades and is a cherished part of the community’s holiday season. Now celebrating its 31st anniversary, Garden d’Lights runs annually from the Saturday after Thanksgiving through New Year’s Eve, delighting guests of all ages with its festive charm and imaginative displays.

$5 nights are Nov 30-Dec 3 and Dec 7-10. Other nights are $10 per person. Children 10 and under are always free.

events.placeLines:
Swoon City, Seattle
1716 NW Market St, Seattle, WA
events.summary: This class will take place at Swoon City.
events.description:
This class will take place at Swoon City. Our address is 1716 NW Market Street, Seattle, WA 98107. It’s at the intersection of 17th and NW Market Street – kitty corner from Mighty-O Donuts.

Please arrive at least 15 minutes before class begins.

If you cannot attend class for any reason, we will offer an exchange to another class currently on our schedule up to 48 hours before the class. After that time, no refunds or exchanges are issued out of respect for our teachers who purchase and prepare supplies based on the number of attendees.

In this 90 minute workshop, you’ll learn the basics of needle felting, as well as all the fun techniques needed to build your very own snow buddy: complete with little bead eyes, a customizable ornament tag, and a scarf of your choice!
After the workshop, you’ll have all the skills you’ll need to continue your felting journey. No experience necessary, beginners welcome.

This workshop involves holding a small needle and repeatedly poking small pieces of wool. If you have any accessibility needs around holding / using a small needle, or any other needs you anticipate, please email gnomoremrfungi@gmail.com in advance of the workshop, and we’ll find a way to make it work for you!

events.summary: Burien Farmer’s Market Farmers markets are an essential part of our economy and community.
events.description:
Burien Farmer’s Market

Farmers markets are an essential part of our economy and community. Shopping at farmers markets helps to support agricultural producers, ensured food access for all and builds connections between producers and consumers.

(Inclement weather rule in-effect: if there is snow present and/or temperature is below 20 degrees, the farmer’s market will be closed. We will post signs at Town Square and on Social Media)

DETAILS:

• The market is open every Thursday.

• Winter Market is open 10am - 4pm (Nov-Apr)

• Summer Market is open 10am - 6pm (May-Oct)

• Most vendors accept and prefer cash but can also process credit and debit cards. You can purchase market tokens with your card at the information booth to use for purchase at all booths. We can also process your Community Gift e-Card - Buy Here

• EBT is accepted! Inquire at the main tent to see how you can receive up to $10 with the SNAP Market Match program

• Enjoy Live Music and Food Tents during the Summer (May to October)

• Vendors rotate often and seasonally, no week is every the same as that last: fruits, vegetables and seasonal produce, jams, honey, preserves, kombucha, baked goods, fresh flowers, cheese, bath and body products, house plants and potted plants, gems & stones, gifts, wine, meat, snacks and art (jewelry, glass works, yard art, cloth and textile crafts, face)

• Pets are allowed on leash

Interested in becoming a VENDOR at the Burien Farmers Market?

Choirs on board the Christmas Ship™ perform to guests aboard, to follow boats also on the lake, and to communities gathered on shore.

events.summary: Burien Farmer’s Market Farmers markets are an essential part of our economy and community.
events.description:
Burien Farmer’s Market

Farmers markets are an essential part of our economy and community. Shopping at farmers markets helps to support agricultural producers, ensured food access for all and builds connections between producers and consumers.

(Inclement weather rule in-effect: if there is snow present and/or temperature is below 20 degrees, the farmer’s market will be closed. We will post signs at Town Square and on Social Media)

DETAILS:

• The market is open every Thursday.

• Winter Market is open 10am - 4pm (Nov-Apr)

• Summer Market is open 10am - 6pm (May-Oct)

• Most vendors accept and prefer cash but can also process credit and debit cards. You can purchase market tokens with your card at the information booth to use for purchase at all booths. We can also process your Community Gift e-Card - Buy Here

• EBT is accepted! Inquire at the main tent to see how you can receive up to $10 with the SNAP Market Match program

• Enjoy Live Music and Food Tents during the Summer (May to October)

• Vendors rotate often and seasonally, no week is every the same as that last: fruits, vegetables and seasonal produce, jams, honey, preserves, kombucha, baked goods, fresh flowers, cheese, bath and body products, house plants and potted plants, gems & stones, gifts, wine, meat, snacks and art (jewelry, glass works, yard art, cloth and textile crafts, face)

• Pets are allowed on leash

Interested in becoming a VENDOR at the Burien Farmers Market?

gemini.wanted:
What this person wants: community happenings in the Seattle area. Night markets and pop-up or
holiday markets; cultural festivals and heritage celebrations (Lunar New Year, Diwali, Día de
Muertos, Chuseok, Obon and the like); street fairs, block parties and parades; seasonal and holiday
events (harvest festivals, pumpkin patches, tree lightings, holiday lights); food and drink
festivals; art walks and art fairs; free outdoor concerts and outdoor movies; farmers markets.
Leave out: ticketed concerts and tours, sports games and watch parties, theater, comedy and dance
performances, bar and club nights, pub crawls, classes, workshops and lectures, conferences and
expos, galas, auctions and fundraising dinners, meetups and support groups, services such as food
banks and clinics, museum exhibitions, restaurant deals and business promotions, and anything sold
through resale ticket sites. A price doesn't decide it: farm harvest festivals, pumpkin patches,
fairs and food festivals often charge admission and are still wanted. Anything that is one of the
kinds above is wanted; when unsure, leave it out.
Categories: NIGHT_MARKET (night, pop-up, holiday and craft markets), CULTURAL (cultural and heritage
festivals), COMMUNITY (street fairs, block parties, parades, general community festivals), SEASONAL
(harvest, Halloween, winter holiday and other seasonal events), FOOD (food and drink festivals), ARTS
(art walks, art fairs), OUTDOOR (free outdoor concerts and movies), FARMERS (farmers markets).
gemini.summaryRule: summary: one plain sentence of at most 20 words saying what happens there. No hype words (amazing, don't miss, must-see), no dates, no prices.
